items.stem: A 95% confidence interval for a mean is (42, 50). What is the sample mean?
items.objective: a symmetric confidence interval is centered on the point estimate

items.stem: A researcher widens a confidence interval from 90% to 99% using the same data. What happens to its width?

choices.text: It depends on the sample mean

items.objective: higher confidence requires a larger critical value and a wider interval

items.stem: A sample of 100 has standard deviation 20. What is the standard error of the mean?
items.objective: compute standard error as s divided by the square root of n

items.stem: A test of H0: mu = 10 gives p = 0.20 at alpha = 0.05. What is the correct conclusion?

choices.text: Fail to reject H0; the data are not strong evidence against mu = 10
There is a 20% chance H0 is true

items.objective: interpret a non-significant result without accepting the null

items.stem: Which changes make a hypothesis test more powerful, holding everything else fixed? Select all that apply.
items.objective: identify the factors that increase statistical power

items.stem: A study finds students who sleep more earn higher grades. Which conclusion is justified?

choices.text: Sleep and grades are associated in this sample

items.objective: distinguish association from causation in observational data
